fact_text: Since 18 October 2024 South Africa adjudicates general work visas and critical skills work visas under a points-based system; besides meeting all other prescribed requirements, an applicant must earn 100 points to be issued a work visa.
evidence_quote: must earn 100 points to obtain a visa

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a job offer plus qualifications automatically secures a South African work visa. Actually since 18 Oct 2024 both the general and critical skills work visa are scored on a 100-point system (occupation, qualification, salary, experience, language). Action: model the candidate's points before applying; below 100 the visa cannot be issued.

fact_text: Under the points-based system an offer of employment is mandatory and salary is scored: an offer above R976,194 gross per annum earns 50 points, while an offer between R650,976 and R976,194 gross per annum earns only 20 points.
evidence_quote: Offer of employment (Mandatory): Above R976,194 gross per annum

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: any local salary is acceptable for a work visa. Actually the offer of employment is mandatory and salary is a scored criterion, with the top band (above R976,194 gross p.a.) worth 50 of the 100 points needed. Action: benchmark the package against the published salary bands, as a low offer can leave the applicant short of 100 points.

entity_title: Points route sets the visa type
fact_text: If the 100-point threshold is reached through an occupation on the critical skills list the applicant may be issued a critical skills work visa; if it is reached by other combined points the applicant may instead be issued a general work visa.
evidence_quote: reached through an occupation contained on the critical skills list, and provided all other prescribed requirements are met, the applicant may be issued with a critical skills work visa

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the applicant chooses between the general and the critical skills work visa. Actually the route is determined by how the 100 points are earned - a critical-skills-list occupation yields the critical skills work visa, any other combination yields the general work visa. Action: check the current critical skills list first, as it changes the visa type and conditions.

entity_title: Occupation must be on the critical skills list
fact_text: For a critical skills work visa the applicant must fall within the critical skills category by selecting one occupation, and that occupation must appear on the latest official Critical Skills List.
evidence_quote: The occupation/critical skill must be on the latest Critical Skills List.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: being highly skilled qualifies you for the critical skills work visa. Actually only occupations named on the current Critical Skills List qualify, and exactly one must be selected. Action: confirm the role maps to a listed occupation on the latest list before choosing this route.

fact_text: A work visa applicant must submit the outcome of their foreign qualifications evaluated by the South African Qualifications Authority (SAQA), translated by a sworn translator into an official language of the Republic.
evidence_quote: Outcome of foreign qualifications evaluated by SAQA and translated by a sworn translator into one of the official languages of the Republic

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the employer's own recognition of a foreign degree is enough. Actually the qualification must be independently evaluated by SAQA and sworn-translated into an official language. Action: start the SAQA evaluation early - it is a common bottleneck; if the outcome is still pending the visa can be issued for one year pending a positive result.

entity_title: Work visa is tied to the employer and role
fact_text: The employer must give a written undertaking to inform the Director-General when the employee is no longer in that employer's employ, or when the employee is employed in a different capacity or role - the work visa is tied to a specific employer and role.
evidence_quote: inform the Director-General upon the employee no longer being in the employ of such employer or when he or she is employed in a different capacity or role

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a work visa lets the holder change jobs or roles freely once in South Africa. Actually it is tied to the specific employer and role, and the employer must notify Home Affairs when employment ends or the role changes. Action: treat a resignation, dismissal or internal role change as a visa event requiring a fresh application.

entity_title: Extensions must be lodged 60 days early in person
fact_text: An application to extend a work visa must be submitted in person no less than 60 days before the applicant's current visa expires.
evidence_quote: the application must be submitted in person, no less than 60 days prior to the expiry date of the applicant's visa

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a visa extension can be filed at any time before expiry, or online. Actually it must be lodged in person and at least 60 days before expiry. Action: diarise the renewal at least 90 days out and book an in-person appointment, as late filing risks the applicant becoming undesirable.

entity_title: Intra-company transfer visa is capped and not renewable
fact_text: An intra-company transfer work visa is issued for a period not exceeding four years and is not renewable - unlike the general and critical skills work visas, which may be issued for up to five years at a time.
evidence_quote: An intra-company transfer work visa shall be issued for a period not exceeding four years and is not renewable.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: an ICT visa can be renewed like other work visas and can be a stepping stone to permanent residence. Actually it is capped at four years and is expressly not renewable. Action: plan the assignment to end within four years or line up a separate work-visa route well before expiry; do not rely on the ICT visa for a long-term stay.

entity_title: ICT holder confined to the transferred position
fact_text: For an intra-company transfer work visa the employer must ensure the foreigner is only employed in the specific position for which the visa was issued.
evidence_quote: a foreigner is only employed in the specific position for which the visa has been issued

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a transferee can take on additional or different duties at the local entity. Actually the ICT visa confines the holder to the one specific position it was issued for. Action: re-apply before moving the transferee into any different role or entity.

entity_title: ICT needs six months' prior employment abroad
fact_text: An intra-company transfer work visa application must be accompanied by the foreigner's contract of employment with the company abroad valid for a period of not less than six months.
evidence_quote: the foreigner's contract of employment with the company abroad valid for a period of not less than six months

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: any new hire can be sent on an intra-company transfer. Actually the transferee must already hold an employment contract with the overseas company valid for at least six months. Action: only nominate staff with 6+ months' tenure abroad for the ICT route; use a general or critical skills work visa for newer hires.

entity_title: Two separate tests can make you a tax resident
fact_text: An individual is treated as a South African tax resident if they are ordinarily resident in South Africa during the year of assessment, or, failing that, if they meet all three requirements of the physical presence day-count test.
evidence_quote: Any individual who is ordinarily resident (common law concept) in South Africa during the year of assessment or, failing which, meets all three requirements of the physical presence test

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: an assignee is only taxed in their home country while on a temporary posting. Actually South Africa taxes residents on worldwide income, and residency arises either by being ordinarily resident or by the physical presence day-count test. Action: assess both tests for each tax year of the assignment, not just the day count.

fact_text: The physical presence test is met only if the individual is present in South Africa for more than 91 days in the current year of assessment, more than 91 days in each of the preceding five years, and more than 915 days in total across those five preceding years.
evidence_quote: 91 days in total during each of the five years of assessment preceding the year of assessment under consideration; and 915 days in total during those five preceding years of assessment

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you only become tax resident after 183 days in a year. Actually residency can arise from a multi-year day count: 91+ days this year, 91+ days in each of the last five years, and 915+ days over those five years. Action: track cumulative days across assignments, as repeated shorter stays can trigger residency.

entity_title: Ordinarily resident turns on where you return
fact_text: For the ordinarily-resident test an individual is ordinarily resident in South Africa if South Africa is the country to which that individual will naturally and as a matter of course return after their wanderings.
evidence_quote: ordinarily resident in South Africa, if South Africa is the country to which that individual will naturally and as a matter of course return after his or her wanderings

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: tax residency is a pure day-count question. Actually the ordinarily-resident test is a facts-and-circumstances common-law test - it can make someone resident even below the day thresholds, based on where their real home and habitual return is. Action: review family, home and intention factors, not just days, when advising on residency.
